title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: When the ground-to-first-excited gap is large and QTM and Raman paths are suppressed, relaxation is mainly Orbach; relaxation through higher doublets (thermally activated QTM) requires strong axiality of both the ground and excited states and can produce barriers of hundreds to more than a thousand kelvin.
explanation: Orbach relaxation follows an Arrhenius law with a barrier equal to the gap to the first excited doublet and is ideally limited by the Debye phonon cutoff, although optical and multi-phonon processes can keep it active beyond that limit. Raman is field-independent and can operate above the Debye temperature; the direct process is field-dependent and linear or quadratic in temperature. TA-QTM through the 3rd, 4th, or 5th doublet is also thermally activated but with a larger gap.
scope: Relaxation dynamics of genuine high-barrier Ln3+ SMMs.
conditions: Large crystal-field gap and shortcut of Raman and ground-state QTM; strong axiality of excited doublets for high-lying TA-QTM.
caveats: The temperature dependence is generally a mixture of processes, so a single Arrhenius barrier can misrepresent the mechanism.
